profile.headline:
FDE
Forward Deployed Engineer
profile.intro: I work on real business needs, from requirements and system development to delivery and iteration. My projects span nonprofits, professional services and international brands. Here is work I have led or contributed to.
profile.about: My project experience spans nonprofits, professional service firms and international brands, with work in requirements analysis, product planning, documentation and development.
profile.personality: I prefer to let my work speak for itself.
profile.background: On projects I lead, I use AI-assisted development and take responsibility for workflow design, testing and maintenance. On team projects, I contribute within the agreed division of work.

P02.process: The client began with two websites before commissioning an internal system. I developed the nonprofit website around the foundation profile, programs and disclosures. Business requirements, product documentation and office system demo interfaces.

The second phase took more than three months, covering development, user training and handover. The client reported less time spent on routine work and lower software costs; no quantified data was provided.
P04.process: Other team members interviewed staff onsite, and I developed the office system from their findings. P09.title: Furniture barcode inventory system
P09.summary: Led a carton-based barcode inventory system, designing receiving, transfers and dispatch with permissions, duplicate-submission handling and correction flows.
story: A carton-based warehouse needs a checkable flow across receiving, transfers, dispatch and corrections. Repeated submissions or retries must not record the same operation twice.
I led requirements and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and maintenance.
Implemented carton scanning, receiving, transfers, dispatch and reversals, with identity checks, duplicate-request handling and insufficient-stock checks.

A complete inventory sequence was checked before duplicate requests, insufficient stock and retries after cancellation. Transfers check source, destination and total quantities; corrections remain linked to the original operation.

Records dated September 8, 2026 cover local and cloud acceptance with virtual inventory. Real phone cameras and factory networks still require on-site validation; these records do not establish factory adoption.

P10.title: Sanitaryware manufacturer inventory system
P10.summary: Independently developed and delivered an inventory system for a large B2B sanitaryware manufacturer, covering requirements, workflow analysis and implementation.
story: The client needed inventory management connected to product variants, purchasing, returns and stocktakes. Quantities and statuses must agree with the actual business operations.

Adapted an existing foundation to inventory workflows across PC and H5 interfaces. The backend includes master data, purchasing, inventory and an overview, with workflow review, test-document and trial-deployment records.

A half-day requirements discussion established the scope. With limited client availability afterward, I used the initial discovery and industry understanding to handle requirements, core development and delivery independently.

Workflow reviews compare documents, stock and inventory transactions. A stocktake example checks the document status, actual quantity reduction and corresponding transaction rather than relying on a success message.
I independently handled requirements, workflow analysis, core development and delivery. The business adaptations are distinguished from the existing foundation.
Delivery took about two months. The client has not yet put the system into full use, so usage outcomes remain unconfirmed.
P10.process: A half-day requirements discussion established inventory management as the core scope. I independently handled requirements, core development and delivery. Limited follow-up availability meant implementation relied on the initial discovery and industry understanding. Delivery took about two months; the client has not yet put the system into full use.

P12.title: Zhijing · AI content workbench
P12.summary: Led a content workbench for furnishing fabrics, organizing product facts, style settings, editing and human review while validating model output, account connection and export separately.
story: Fabric businesses need content based on product images, specifications and account style. Human review remains part of the flow to keep content aligned with product facts.
I led requirements and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and maintenance.
The local workbench includes initial setup, style confirmation, product input, editing, human review and export paths. The image shows the product-input interface.
Product facts, content capabilities, human approval and output paths are organized and validated separately. A successful account connection is not treated as evidence of a complete generation flow.
Records from August 2026 cover a real text probe and account login, confirmation, restart, disconnection and login again. A historical full-content test failed at delivery of the first image.

The available public material does not include a passing end-to-end generation or RED publishing receipt. This case presents the workbench and partial verification, without claiming stable automatic generation or publishing.
P12.process: I led requirements and workflow design for furnishing-fabric content and used AI-assisted development for a local workbench. Product facts and style are confirmed before editing and human review. Available evidence covers the interface and historical partial tests; complete image-and-copy generation and platform publishing require separate validation.

P15.title: PetSocial (now HelloTail)
P15.summary: Developed pet profiles, photo displays, discovery invitations and chat, handling message sending and recovery after restart with a separate experience demo.
story: Pet profiles provide a starting point for discovery, invitations, owner connections and text conversations.
I developed the entire project, including pet profiles and photos, discovery invitations, owner connections, chat and message-recovery features.

The native iOS app connects profile, discovery and chat flows, with message state and restart recovery. The separate VisualDemo presents UI and interactions; it does not replace native feature or device verification.

UI experience, real services and device state are checked separately. An October 5, 2026 regression on my iPhone covered profiles, connections and chat history. A technical test message appeared once; after terminating and restarting the app, the session and sent message were restored from the service.

The current native candidate is iterating as HelloTail, with local build, installation on my device and partial-verification records. The historical recovery example does not establish cross-device receipt, notification delivery or full feature acceptance.

The image still comes from the separate VisualDemo. Physical-device performance and release completion need their own validation; a demo image or installation record is not proof of an App Store release.
P15.process: I developed this native iOS pet-social project, now iterating under the name HelloTail, connecting pet profiles, discovery invitations and chat. A separate VisualDemo presents the experience. The cover comes from that demo; native implementation and device validation are described separately.
